'''''Linaria almadensis''''' is a species of [[Linaria|toadflax]] in the plantain family [[Plantaginaceae]], [[endemic]] to [[Portugal]], specifically the coastal cliffs of [[Almada]], (from where the species name comes) south of [[Lisbon]]. First described in 2026 by João Farminhão, it inhabits a very restricted area spanning only the sandy walls close to carbonate rocks in the cliffs pointed to the [[Tagus]] river with samples collected from rocks close to the [[Christ the King (Almada)|Cristo Rei]] monument.<ref>{{cite web |title=Linaria almadensis - Nova espécie de planta descoberta nas arribas do Tejo |url=https://www.cm-almada.pt/linaria-almadensis-nova-especie-de-planta-descoberta-nas-arribas-do-tejo |publisher=[[Almada]] |access-date=26 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Joana |date=2026-01-26 |title=New species discovered by João Farminhão (CFE/TERRA) opposite the city of Lisbon |url=https://labterra.pt/new-species-discovered-by-joao-farminhao-cfe-terra-opposite-the-city-of-lisbon/ |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=Lab Terra |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Description ==

Its identifying features include green leaves with an obtuse-apiculate apex, densely gladular-pubescent inflorence axis, and orange corolla palate with a wider corolla tube in its lateral section.<ref name="Farminhão 2026">{{cite journal |last=Farminhão |first=J. |date=2026 |title=''Linaria almadensis'' (Plantaginaceae, Antirrhineae): a highly threatened new toadflax endemic to the Tagus mouth cliffs, opposite Lisbon (Portugal) |journal=Botany Letters |pages=1-17 |doi=10.1080/23818107.2025.2608732 |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/23818107.2025.2608732|url-access=subscription }}</ref> It blooms in April-May with frutification happening in May, and it has been found in altitudes between {{cvt|20 and 89|m}} [[above sea level]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=26 January 2026 |author=Flora-On |title=''Linaria almadensis'' |url=http://www.flora-on.pt/#/0-AY2}}<!-- auto-translated from Portuguese by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> It is a perennial herb, with branched roots and heteromorphic green stems between {{cvt|26 and 48|cm}} long. Its leaves come in whorls of 3-4 becoming alternate towards the inflorescence. Its corolla has 7 upper petals and tube is yellowish-white, palate orangey-yellow, spur yellowish-white or violet, with conspicuous dark veins.<ref name="Farminhão 2026" />

== Distribution and habitat ==

Only 34 individuals were recorded living on site within an EOO of {{cvt|16|km2}}, although more could be found on more difficult terrain between [[Cacilhas]] and [[Trafaria]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Descoberta nova espécie de planta para a ciência em arribas do Tejo, frente a Lisboa |url=https://wilder.pt/historias/descoberta-nova-especie-de-planta-para-a-ciencia-em-arribas-do-tejo-frente-a-lisboa |publisher=[[Wilder]] |access-date=26 January 2026}}</ref> It has been preliminarily attributed the status of Critically Endangered due to its restricted distribution, small confirmed numbers and threats to its natural habitat such as invasive species like ''[[Arundo donax]] L.'', ''[[Paraserianthes lophantha]]'' and ''[[Tropaeolum majus]] L.''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Descoberta nova espécie de planta endémica das arribas do Gargalo do Tejo |url=https://noticias.uc.pt/artigos/descoberta-nova-especie-de-planta-endemica-das-arribas-do-gargalo-do-tejo/ |publisher=[[Notícias UC]] |access-date=26 January 2026}}</ref>

== History ==
''Linaria almadensis'' had been previously confused with other species from the ''[[Linaria]]'' genus such as ''[[Linaria polygalifolia]]'', ''[[Linaria supina]]'', ''[[Linaria tristis]]'', and ''[[Linaria marginata]]''. It was first collected in 1843 by the [[Austro-Hungarian]] [[botanist]] [[Friedrich Martin Josef Welwitsch]] (1806–1872), and in 1881 by the [[Portuguese people|Portuguese]] gardener and botanical explorer António Ricardo da Cunha (1830–1893). <ref name="Farminhão 2026" />
